messages.subject: Ensuring absence observations are included
parts:
Apologies if this question has already been asked - I've looked all over SO and read through the Distance Vignette but still not sure how to do this. 

A number of my transect surveys had no observations of the target species. How do I include these absences in my data set for the ds() ? Do I simply need to give a value of NA in the 'distance' column for that transect row?
e.g.
`` 
read_csv("Region.Label, Area, Sample.Label, Effort, distance
                   GUAVA, 0, GUAVA01, 100, NA")
``
Thank you for your help in advance! 
Allie

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Ensuring absence observations are included
parts:
Alex

Thanks for your question.  You are correct that transects without detections do need to be present in the data frame for analysis.  There is no measured distances if there were no detections, so the value placed into the distance column is `NA`.

Have a look at the point transect vignette

http://examples.distancesampling.org/Distance-points/pointtransects-distill.html#make-the-data-available-for-r-session

showing the first several rows of the 1980 data frame.  All those distances are `NA` indicating Savanna sparrows were not detected on the first six point transects in the survey.
